question:
The probability distribution of a random variable X is given as :

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline X & 1 & 2 & 3 & 2\lambda & 3\lambda & 4\lambda \\ \hline P(X) & \frac{11}{30} & \frac{1}{15} & \frac{1}{10} & \frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{15} & \frac{1}{10} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

(i) Calculate λ, if $E(X)=3.2$. (ii) Find $P(X>1)$.
explanation:
**Step 1:** The mathematical formula for the expectation value is defined as $E(X) = \sum x_i P(x_i)$. Substituting our table values gives $E(X) = 1(\frac{11}{30}) + 2(\frac{2}{30}) + 3(\frac{3}{30}) + 2\lambda(\frac{9}{30}) + 3\lambda(\frac{2}{30}) + 4\lambda(\frac{3}{30})$. This simplifies to $E(X) = \frac{24 + 36\lambda}{30}$.
**Step 2:** We are given that $E(X) = 3.2 = \frac{96}{30}$. Equating the two expressions yields $24 + 36\lambda = 96 \implies 36\lambda = 72 \implies \lambda = 2$. This completes part (i) of the problem.
**Step 3:** For part (ii), we calculate $P(X > 1)$ using the complement property: $P(X > 1) = 1 - P(X = 1)$. Substituting the table value gives $1 - \frac{11}{30} = \frac{19}{30}$.
